rv.q: Leavitt has written a seriously comic gem, one that earns every laugh while quietly preparing the ground for moments of genuine emotional force.
Sukkot is very well worth the watching.
Sukkot at 59E59 to emerge as that rare, lovely beast, a dysfunctional family dramedy that feels both fresh and believable.

cn.t: Critics praise this satisfying comedy-drama about a grieving widower honoring his late Jewish wife by celebrating Sukkot, finding it a perceptive exploration of grief as a complex, unruly emotion rather than a singular feeling.
